example: I wake up at seven, but I stay in bed for ten more minutes.
pattern: Intransitive wake up: I wake up at seven. For another person use wake someone up; pronouns go between wake and up: wake me up.
register: Everyday; intransitive here; also transitive and separable
frequencyEvidence: Cambridge labels the stop-sleeping sense A1. Oxford confirms the same everyday sense and distinguishes intransitive wake up from transitive wake someone up; no numeric frequency claim.

check.question: Does the speaker leave bed immediately?
check.explanation: The speaker stays in bed for ten more minutes.

practice.personalUse: Say when you wake up on a workday.
practice.laterReview: Your alarm rings at seven but you leave bed at seven ten. Say when you wake up and when you get up.
